answer:
**Fix alert noise first.** Rotation size (6) is fine, 10 pages/wk mostly false is the problem.

**Wk 1: audit**
- Pull last 30-60 days of pages, tag each: actionable / false / duplicate / self-resolved.
- Rank by alert rule; typically 3-5 rules cause 60-80% of the noise.

**Wk 1-2: kill or fix top offenders**
- No human action needed → delete or demote to ticket/Slack.
- Self-resolves → add a `for:` duration (5-10 min) or auto-remediate.
- Flapping → hysteresis, or widen the threshold.
- Cause-based (CPU, disk %, single-host) → replace w/ symptom-based (user-facing error rate, latency, SLO burn rate).
- Duplicates → group or dedupe, add dependency inhibition.

**Rule going forward**
- Page only if urgent, actionable & user-impacting; everything else is a ticket.
- Every page has a runbook & owner.
- Target ≤2 pages per on-call shift (Google SRE benchmark).

**Process**
- Weekly on-call handoff reviews every page: fix, tune, or delete.
- On-call engineer does no feature work; spare time goes to alert fixes.
- Give comp time after any night page.
- Make the top noisy alerts roadmap work, not side work.

**Metrics:** pages/wk, % actionable (target >80%), off-hours pages.

Don't start by adding people, changing rotation length, or buying tooling; none of them fix false alarms.
